claims: Named native-only-mocked tests require the numeric wait() result, reject missing/invalid/negative running-sentinel returns even when a stale handle contains zero, and preserve valid nonnegative native statuses without an unsigned-byte cap.
Named tests preserve existing timeout124 and native-error127 behavior without command replay.

Named lifecycle regressions propagate native connection/termination failures, validate container identity, require exact public true acknowledgement, and avoid reconnecting a native handle already connected by lookup.
limitations: Only named local command and lifecycle regression cases are covered; live native behavior, other operations and full capability coverage remain unverified.
No clean dependency installation or native-provider execution was performed; the existing installed dependency store was reused.
Installed native SDK contracts were inspected at the recorded version; compatibility throughout the declared dependency range is unverified.
Ordinary native errors retain the existing synthetic exit127 policy; protocol rejection does not itself guarantee remote cleanup or process-tree reaping.
The native process constructor may normalize missing completed wire status to zero before the adapter sees it; these checks are not raw-wire validation.
Launch, output reads and best-effort remote kill are not proven to fit a hard elapsed-time bound; remote termination and reaping remain unverified.

Public terminate Boolean-normalizes its wire acknowledgement, and connection errors lack an authoritative public absence discriminator. No raw-wire, observed absence or physical-termination claim; profile remains cleanup-blocked.
